pr_title: net: ieee802154: software destination MAC address filtering
pr_body:
IEEE802.15.4 software destination address filtering for drivers not implementing `IEEE802154_HW_FILTER` (e.g., `ieee802154_cc13xx_cc26xx_subg`).

Fixes #36267.

issue_context.title: net: ieee802154: software address filtering
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'm currently developing the firmware for a CC13x2-based wireless sensor board using its sub-GHz radio.
Currently, the `ieee802154_cc13xx_cc26xx_subg` driver does not support hardware-based address filtering and I could not figure out a way to do it (since it uses the `CMD_PROP_*` proprietary subg protocol commands tricked to receive IEEE 802.15.4 frames).
So I have 3 devices up and running with a shell, one sends a frame to a specific IEEE extended MAC address and all other devices (even the ones that don't match the frame's destination address) will happily bring it to the upper IPv6 subsystem which will believe the packet needs to be routed (thus sending it again). Not sure if the latter would be a separate bug or routing process functioning as expected.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The easiest solution to this would be to implement software address filtering if the driver does not advertise IEEE802154_HW_FILTER capability (or always).

Since this is quite a blocker for me, I implemented a simple software filtering procedure for extended MAC addresses and tested this.
I'll submit a pull request shortly. Thanks.
